answers.answer: The draw deck contains the 12 Speed cards, 3 Starting Upgrade cards, and 3 Stress cards shuffled together. Put the 6 Heat cards face up on the Engine spot, set the Gear pawn to 1st gear, and draw 7 cards.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–6 and 9: shuffle those cards into the draw deck; place 6 Heat face up on Engine; set to 1st; draw 7.

answers.answer: Yes, you may stay in your gear. You may shift two positions (1st to 3rd) by immediately paying 1 Heat during Shift Gears, moving that Heat from your Engine to your discard pile. You must have it available then.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, step 1: stay or shift one for free; two positions costs 1 Heat immediately during this step, from Engine to discard.

answers.answer: No. In 3rd gear you must commit 3 cards from hand, face down; the number equals your gear.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, step 2: play cards from hand face down equal to gear number (3rd gear = 3).

answers.answer: Steps 1 and 2 are simultaneous for all players, in that order. Everyone must finish both before step 3 begins. Then players take turns front car first, and each player completes steps 3–9 before the next starts. If side by side, the car closest to the Race Line acts first.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: simultaneous phase steps 1–2; sequential phase steps 3–9, front car first; side-by-side Race Line tie-break.

answers.answer: Cars do not block passage. If your destination space is full, place your car in the first free spot behind the blocking cars. If placing in a space, use the spot closest to the Race Line when it is available.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Blocked Movement: cars never block passage; full destination goes in first free spot behind. Reveal & Move: place closest to Race Line if available.

answers.answer: Discard the flipped Heat and Starting Upgrade cards immediately as non-Speed cards. The Speed 3 card goes in your Play Area on top of the played Stress card and supplies speed 3 for it; the played Stress remains underneath. Resolve every played Stress before moving on to Adrenaline.
answers.evidence: Stress Cards: discard each flipped non-Speed card, including Heat and Starting Upgrade; found Speed card goes atop Stress and provides its speed; resolve all Stress before Adrenaline.

answers.answer: In a five-car race, the last two cars to move receive Adrenaline (eligibility is based on the number that started). Each can use one extra Cooldown and add 1 extra speed, either, both, or neither. The extra speed may be taken before or after Boost. Unused Adrenaline cannot be saved.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Adrenaline: with 5 or more starting cars, last two receive benefits; extra Cooldown and speed; speed before/after Boost; unused cannot be saved.

answers.answer: Yes. In 2nd gear you have Cooldown allowance 1, so during React you may move one Heat card from hand to Engine, then immediately spend it to Boost by paying it from Engine to discard. Cooldown and Boost can be activated in any order, and Cooldown before Boost is explicitly allowed.
answers.evidence: React: activate Cooldown and/or Boost in any order; may Cooldown Heat into Engine, then immediately spend it to Boost. Cooldown: 2nd gear provides 1.

answers.answer: You may Boost once per turn during React. It costs 1 Heat from Engine to discard; with no Engine Heat you cannot Boost unless you first Cooldown a Heat card from hand during React. Flip until a Speed card appears, discarding each non-Speed card; add that Speed card and move its value. Boost speed counts for corner checks.
answers.evidence: Boost section: once per turn during React; pay 1 Engine Heat; flip to Speed card; boost increases total speed for corner checks. Paying Heat section allows prior Cooldown.

answers.answer: Slipstream is optional. Check the corner using total speed 6; Slipstream movement is excluded from corner-check speed. With limit 4, the excess is 2, so pay 2 Heat if able.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: optionally move 2; does not increase speed for corner checks. Check Corner: pay Heat equal to excess speed.

answers.answer: Check both corners, in the order crossed. Use speed 8 for each: pay 2 for the limit-6 corner and 4 for the limit-4 corner, for 6 Heat altogether.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: check every Corner Line crossed in order; for each separately use same total speed and pay excess.

answers.answer: You cannot pay the 3 Heat required with only 2, so spin out: move all remaining Engine Heat to your discard pile, return to the first available space before the corner, take 2 extra Stress cards directly into your hand (4th gear), and set your gear to 1st.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Spin Out: all remaining Engine Heat to discard; return before triggering corner; 2 Stress in hand for 3rd/4th; set to 1st.

answers.answer: You may discard unwanted Speed cards, but not Stress or Heat cards. You may not browse any discard pile, including your own; only the top card of each pile is public knowledge.
answers.evidence: Step 8 Discard: may discard unwanted cards but never Stress or Heat; nobody may browse any pile; only top card is public knowledge.

answers.answer: Move all Play Area cards to your discard pile, then draw only enough cards to bring your hand back to 7, not seven additional cards.
answers.evidence: Step 9 Replenish Hand states exactly this.

answers.answer: Shuffle your discard pile into a new draw deck immediately, then continue the interrupted flips. Do not include cards still in your Play Area; they have not yet been discarded.
answers.evidence: Running Out of Cards: shuffle discard into new draw deck and continue interrupted draws/flips; do not include Play Area cards.

answers.answer: When paying Heat, move it from Engine to discard. It can cycle from discard to draw deck to hand, and returns to Engine only via Cooldown. Heat cannot normally be played or voluntarily discarded from hand.
answers.evidence: Paying Heat; Heat Card Cycle; final Special Rules bullet on hand Heat.

answers.answer: In 4th gear you need four committed cards. Commit the two playable cards you can and fill the remaining two slots with Heat cards in your Play Area. You move zero spaces, set your gear to 1st, discard all committed cards including the covering Heat, and skip directly to step 9. You skip React, so cannot Cooldown or Boost this turn.
answers.evidence: Cluttered Hand: commit playable cards and fill remaining slots with Heat; move zero; set 1st; discard all committed; skip to step 9 and React.

answers.answer: The first to cross does not automatically win if multiple cars finish in the same round. The car furthest ahead wins; if tied side by side, closest to Race Line breaks the tie. At round end, remove all cars that crossed the final finish line and place them in finishing order on the Hall of Fame.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: same-round finishers ranked furthest ahead, Race Line breaks ties; at round end remove finishers to Hall of Fame.

answers.answer: No, on the final lap you cannot Slipstream across the finish line, or Slipstream after crossing it. After crossing the final finish line, ignore speed limits of corners beyond it and move as far as you can.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions and Slipstream step: final-lap crossing/after-crossing restriction; ignore corners beyond final finish.

answers.answer: Both remaining cars receive Adrenaline, because a race that started with 5 or more cars gives it to the last two to move. The starting count of six determines eligibility, even after finishers leave.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: if race started with 5 or more, last two receive benefits; use number of cars that started even after finishers leave.

answers.answer: Use the lap count printed on the selected board. The USA track normally uses 2 laps; for a first USA learning race, the summary suggests racing just 1 lap.
answers.evidence: Setup step 1: use laps printed on board; USA learning race may be 1 lap instead of its normal 2.

answers.answer: Do not assume every track uses exactly 6 Heat and 3 Stress. Check the board for how many Heat and Stress cards each player adds; the summary says typically 6 Heat and 3 Stress.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: check board for counts, typically 6 Heat and 3 Stress.

answers.answer: Randomly assign participating cars to the starting grid, placing them one at a time and filling numbered spots in ascending order. This determines first-round order; players do not choose preferred starting positions.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8 states random assignment, numbered spots ascending, determines order, and players do not choose positions.

answers.answer: Place the remaining Stress cards face up near the board as a reserve.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: remaining Stress cards face up near board as reserve.

answers.answer: The optional handicap is for an experienced driver to remove 1 or 2 Heat from their own car to level the playing field.
answers.evidence: Optional handicap: experienced driver may remove 1 or 2 Heat from own car.

answers.answer: The largest shift is two positions in one step. You may shift 1st to 3rd for 1 Heat, but not directly from 1st to 4th.
answers.evidence: Shift Gears allows shifting up or down one free or two positions by paying 1 Heat; reference gives examples 1st to 3rd or 2nd to 4th.

answers.answer: No. The 1 Heat cost for shifting two positions must be available and paid immediately during Shift Gears from Engine to discard. Heat in hand cannot pay it; later React Cooldown cannot pay a past shift cost.
answers.evidence: Shift Gears: immediately paying 1 Heat during this step, moving it from Engine to discard; must have it available. Paying Heat: hand Heat cannot pay.

answers.answer: Resolve each played Stress card by flipping until a Speed card appears, discarding non-Speed cards for each sequence. The total speed is 3 + 4 + 2 = 9. The found Speed 3 and Speed 4 cards provide the Stress cards' speed; they are not additional cards committed from hand.
answers.evidence: Stress Cards: for each Stress, flip until Speed, place found Speed atop played Stress and use its value; step 2 commits cards from hand equal to gear.

answers.answer: No. You must move forward exactly the total speed and cannot voluntarily stop short to avoid a corner.
answers.evidence: Reveal & Move: move exactly the sum; cannot voluntarily stop short to avoid a corner.

answers.answer: Use total speed 8 for the corner check, even though blocked movement shortened your actual movement to 5 spaces. With limit 6, pay 2 Heat if able.
answers.evidence: Check Corner uses total speed for the round; Blocked Movement permits shorter movement if destination is full.

answers.answer: No. A corner check is triggered by crossing a Corner Line; merely stopping before it does not require a payment.
answers.evidence: Track Lines: a Corner Line triggers a corner check when crossed; step 7 checks Corner Lines crossed this turn.

answers.answer: No Heat is due at speed 6 or below against a limit of 6, so there is no spin out just because Engine is empty. Payment is required only for speed above the limit.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: pay Heat equal to excess, if any; if speed does not exceed limit, pay nothing.

answers.answer: You successfully pay the required 3 Heat and continue. Spin Out occurs when you cannot pay enough Heat, not merely because payment empties the Engine.
answers.evidence: Spin Out: if you cannot pay enough Heat for a corner; Paying Heat moves the required cards from Engine to discard.

answers.answer: At the first corner (limit 6), speed 8 requires 2 Heat, leaving 3. At the second (limit 4), 4 Heat are required, so that second corner causes the spin out. Move all remaining 3 Heat to discard, return to the first available space before that corner, take 2 Stress cards directly into your hand (4th gear), and set gear to 1st.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: separately pay excess at each corner in order. Spin Out: remaining Heat to discard, return before corner causing spin out, 2 Stress in hand in 3rd/4th gear, set 1st.

answers.answer: Take 1 extra Stress card directly into your hand, then move your Gear pawn to 1st gear.
answers.evidence: Spin Out: 1 extra Stress directly into hand in 1st/2nd gear; then set gear to 1st.

answers.answer: 1st gear provides Cooldown 3; Adrenaline adds 1, for a maximum of 4 Heat cooled from hand. You are not forced to use it all; cooling fewer or none is allowed.
answers.evidence: Cooldown: 1st gear allowance 3; Adrenaline adds 1; cooling fewer or none is allowed.

answers.answer: Yes. You may decline the extra speed and still use the extra Cooldown; either benefit, both, or neither may be used.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: may use either benefit, both, or neither; declining extra speed does not prevent extra Cooldown.

answers.answer: Yes. Eligibility follows turn order/last car(s) to move, so your move into the lead does not remove eligibility. In a four-car race, only the last car to move receives Adrenaline; the second-to-last does not, because the two-car rule applies only when at least five cars started.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: last car to move gets access; last two only if race started with 5 or more cars.

answers.answer: You qualify if you end next to another car or in the space immediately behind a car. If neither, you do not qualify.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: if you end next to another car or in the space immediately behind a car, optionally move 2 spaces.

answers.answer: Yes. Slipstream eligibility is based on where you end after the React step, so a Boost during React that puts you immediately behind a car can qualify you at the Slipstream step.
answers.evidence: Turn order places React before Slipstream, and Slipstream eligibility applies if you end next to or immediately behind a car. The summary does not explicitly discuss a Boost changing eligibility.

answers.answer: Just one two-space Slipstream move. Qualifying next to or behind multiple cars does not multiply it.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: qualifying next to or behind multiple cars does not multiply this move.

answers.answer: Slipstream does not let you share an occupied spot. Use the normal Blocked Movement placement rule for a full landing space, placing in the first free spot behind the blocking cars. Any shortened movement still does not change corner-check speed.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: full landing space uses normal Blocked Movement; no sharing and shorter movement does not change corner-check speed.

answers.answer: No. Check both corners crossed, in order, but ignore speed limits only for corners beyond the final finish line. Pay 4 Heat for the limit-4 corner before the line; no Heat for the limit-3 corner beyond it, for 4 total.
answers.evidence: Check Corner checks every crossed line; final lap rules ignore speed limits of corners beyond the final finish line.

answers.answer: Yes, an otherwise legal Slipstream may cross the start/finish line on an intermediate lap. Normal corner speed limits still apply beyond it.
answers.evidence: Scoring: on intermediate laps, otherwise legal Slipstream may cross start/finish, and normal corner limits apply beyond it.

answers.answer: The remaining cars continue; the round-end procedure removes cars that crossed the final finish line, and play continues until all cars finish.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: at round end remove finishers and continue playing until all cars finish.

answers.answer: In the core game, crossing a Corner Line triggers a corner check. The Legends Line alone does not trigger corner payment; it is used only in advanced play.
answers.evidence: Track Lines: Corner Line triggers a check in core game; Legends Line is used only in advanced play and is not a core payment trigger.

answers.answer: No. Gear shifting happens before committing cards. If you shift from 3rd down to 2nd, you commit two cards for the current 2nd gear; with two playable cards, you do not trigger Cluttered Hand.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: shift gears in step 1, then play cards equal to gear in step 2. Cluttered Hand applies if too few playable cards for your gear.
